changes.before: Nonetheless, recent indicators point to continuing weakness in overall labor market conditions, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
changes.after: While indicators point to some improvement in overall labor market conditions, the unemployment rate remains elevated.

changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that economic growth strengthened somewhat in the third quarter, reflecting in part a reversal of the temporary factors that had weighed on growth earlier in the year.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November suggests that the economy has been expanding moderately, notwithstanding some apparent slowing in global growth.

changes.before: Business investment in equipment and software has continued to expand, but investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.
changes.after: Household spending has continued to advance, but business fixed investment appears to be increasing less rapidly and the housing sector remains depressed.

changes.before: Moreover, there are significant downside risks to the economic outlook, including strains in global financial markets.
changes.after: Strains in global financial markets continue to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.

changes.before: Inflation appears to have moderated since earlier in the year as prices of energy and some commodities have declined from their peaks.
changes.after: Inflation has moderated since earlier in the year, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.

parsed.rationale: Policy actions and the mid-2013 forward guidance are unchanged, with only modest offsetting tweaks: a better labor-market read against slower investment, global slowing, and more emphasized financial-strain risks. Net signal is essentially unchanged.

spans.quote: Nonetheless, recent indicators point to continuing weakness in overall labor market conditions, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.

Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that economic growth strengthened somewhat in the third quarter, reflecting in part a reversal of the temporary factors that had weighed on growth earlier in the year.
Business investment in equipment and software has continued to expand, but investment in nonresidential structures is still weak, and the housing sector remains depressed.
Moreover, there are significant downside risks to the economic outlook, including strains in global financial markets.
Inflation appears to have moderated since earlier in the year as prices of energy and some commodities have declined from their peaks.
While indicators point to some improvement in overall labor market conditions, the unemployment rate remains elevated.
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November suggests that the economy has been expanding moderately, notwithstanding some apparent slowing in global growth.
Household spending has continued to advance, but business fixed investment appears to be increasing less rapidly and the housing sector remains depressed.
Strains in global financial markets continue to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.
Inflation has moderated since earlier in the year, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
